Everything for the workshop is in one download. We'll set it up together at the start of the session, so there's nothing you need to do in advance. The steps are written out below so you can find them again later, or redo the setup on another computer.

::: {.lab-apply}
[Download the workshop folder (.zip)](files/r-workshop/r-workshop-1.zip){.btn-apply}
:::

The zip contains a single folder, `r-workshop-1`, holding three things:

``` text
r-workshop-1/
├── R-Workshop-1.Rproj          the RStudio project file
├── workshop1_student.qmd       the workbook you'll write in
└── data/
    └── workshop1_survey.csv    the dataset (250 responses)
```

## Setting it up

We'll walk through this together, but here it is in writing.

**1. Unzip it.** Double-click the download. On Windows, open the zip and choose *Extract All* --- if you skip this and work inside the zip preview, nothing will save properly.

**2. Move the whole folder somewhere you'll find it again.** Not Downloads. Put `r-workshop-1` in your Documents folder, or wherever you keep coursework. We'll work out of this same folder for the rest of the workshop, and Downloads is the first place things get lost or auto-cleared.

**3. Open it by double-clicking `R-Workshop-1.Rproj`.** Not the `.qmd` file. Opening the `.Rproj` is what tells RStudio which folder is the project, and that's what makes `data/workshop1_survey.csv` work as a path. If you open the workbook on its own, the data won't load.

## Keep the folder together

The three items have to stay in the same folder, arranged the way they arrived. The workbook asks R to read `data/workshop1_survey.csv`, which means "starting from the project folder, look inside `data` for that file." Move the CSV to your desktop, or pull the workbook out on its own, and that path stops pointing at anything.

You can move or rename the whole `r-workshop-1` folder freely --- that's the point of a project. Just move it as one piece.

## Installing R and RStudio

If you don't already have them, you need both, in this order:

1. **[R](https://cloud.r-project.org/)** --- the language itself.
2. **[RStudio Desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/)** --- the editor we'll use. It expects R to already be there.

The packages we use get installed by running this line in the RStudio Console:

```r
install.packages("tidyverse")
```

It takes a few minutes and prints a lot of text. That's normal.

## If something goes wrong

- **`could not find function "read_csv"`** --- run `library(tidyverse)` first.
- **`cannot open file 'data/workshop1_survey.csv'`** --- you almost certainly opened the `.qmd` directly instead of the `.Rproj`. Close RStudio, double-click `R-Workshop-1.Rproj`, and reopen the workbook from the Files pane.
- **Nothing saves, or files keep disappearing** --- you're working inside the zip. Extract it properly and move the folder out of Downloads.

Just bring a laptop. We'll handle the rest in the session.
